title: Advanced Audience Framing and Insight Architecture
description: Master the art of reframing identical datasets for different stakeholders while maintaining analytical integrity.

interactions.prompt: When presenting the same churn data to these two audiences, which framing distinction matters most?

options.text: CFO sees revenue impact; Product VP sees feature-level retention drivers
Use simpler charts for the CFO and complex ones for Product
Show both audiences the same funnel with different titles
Lead with methodology for CFO, lead with recommendations for Product

interactions.teachingPreamble: Audience framing isn't about dumbing data down—it's about aligning the same truth to different decision contexts. When Spotify's data team presents churn analysis, the CFO needs to understand LTV erosion by cohort, while the Product VP needs to see which playlist engagement thresholds predict retention. Same underlying dataset, entirely different narrative spines.

interactions.prompt: Shopify Q3 data: Enterprise plan churn dropped 18%, but enterprise revenue fell 9%. SMB churn rose 4%, yet SMB revenue grew 22%. Total customer count is flat. What's the real story?

options.text: Churn is improving overall so the business is healthy
Enterprise customers are downgrading plans, masking revenue risk behind low churn
SMB growth is cannibalizing the enterprise segment
Flat customer count means growth has stalled across both segments

chartData.title: Q3 Key Metrics: Churn vs Revenue Growth by Segment

interactions.prompt: You need to present a failed A/B test (no significant lift) to leadership expecting positive results. What's the strongest narrative approach?

options.text: Bury the null result inside a broader quarterly trends overview
Frame the null result as a constraint that narrows the solution space strategically
Highlight the methodology was sound and recommend simply re-running the test
Pivot entirely to a different metric where the variant performed better

interactions.teachingPreamble: The most advanced data storytelling skill is narrating negative or null results without losing credibility or momentum. Netflix's experimentation team frames null results as 'eliminated hypotheses'—each one reducing uncertainty about where the real lever exists. The narrative structure shifts from 'Here's what worked' to 'Here's what we now know, and here's where that points us next.'

interactions.prompt: In data storytelling, the 'So What? → Now What?' framework ensures every insight is paired with a ____, preventing the common trap of presenting analysis without actionable direction.

options.text: Visualization
Statistical confidence interval
Decision recommendation
Benchmark comparison

interactions.prompt: You're presenting to Uber's board: rider growth is up 30% but revenue per ride dropped 21% due to aggressive promotions. You have one opening slide. Do you lead with the growth narrative or the unit economics concern?

options.text: Lead with growth—it's the board's strategic priority—then transition to economics
Lead with unit economics decline—boards respect facing hard truths first
Lead with a combined metric like revenue growth rate to show both
Lead with competitive context showing market share gains justify the tradeoff

interactions.prompt: Which technique best prevents the 'insight extraction' failure where analysts surface correlations that executives misinterpret as causal?

options.text: Always include p-values and confidence intervals on every slide
Use a causal framing ladder: correlation → quasi-experiment → true experiment
Avoid showing correlations entirely and only present experimental results
Add a disclaimer footnote about correlation versus causation on each chart

interactions.teachingPreamble: Airbnb's data science team uses an 'evidence hierarchy' in every presentation: they explicitly label each insight by its causal strength. A correlation between Superhost status and booking rate is labeled 'observational association,' while an A/B test result on search ranking is labeled 'causal estimate.' This prevents executives from treating all data points as equally actionable and focuses investment on the highest-confidence findings.

interactions.prompt: You're structuring a 15-minute data story for Stripe's CPO about declining API adoption among mid-market customers. Rank these narrative elements from first to last in your presentation.

options.text: Detailed cohort analysis showing adoption curves by company size
The strategic stakes: mid-market is 40% of pipeline revenue
Three prioritized recommendations with expected impact ranges
Root cause analysis linking decline to onboarding friction and competitor moves

interactions.prompt: Mid-presentation, the CPO reveals Stripe just acquired a competitor whose mid-market product solves the onboarding friction you identified. How do you pivot your data story in real time?

options.text: Stick to your original recommendations since your data still holds
Reframe your cohort data as a migration baseline for acquired customers
Acknowledge the change and offer to redo the full analysis post-acquisition
Pivot to the competitor analysis slide and highlight integration risks

interactions.priorContext: You had just presented root cause analysis showing onboarding friction as the primary driver of mid-market decline, with recommendations to rebuild the onboarding flow. The CPO's acquisition news fundamentally changes the solution landscape—your friction diagnosis is still valid, but your recommendations are now partially obsolete.
